items.title: GPT-5.6 used a prompt to solve a 30-year-old problem in convex optimization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: GPT-5.6 applied a specific prompt to close a longstanding 30-year gap in the field of convex optimization, marking a significant advancement in mathematical problem-solving. This development was discussed in online math communities following OpenAI's announcement related to control theory and optimization proofs. The breakthrough highlights the growing capability of AI models to contribute to complex mathematical research and problem-solving tasks.

This analysis provides insight into the evolving role of AI within the Stack Overflow community.

items.title: Fable 5 outperforms GPT-5.6 Sol on a complex NP-hard fiber-network design problem; /goal mode shows mixed impact [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A benchmark test compared Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on an unpublished NP-hard optimization problem involving fiber-network design for French cities. Fable 5 delivered the best and most consistent solutions, surpassing GPT-5.6 Sol by a significant margin. The experiment also evaluated the effect of the models' native /goal mode, finding it sometimes improved results but was not a decisive factor. The problem required connecting distribution points and terminals with loops and branches under strict constraints, with the objective of minimizing total cable length. The search space was extremely large, with an estimated lower bound of 10^1223 possible solutions. The study included multiple runs and detailed analysis of the /goal command implementations in Claude Code and Codex, revealing different mechanisms and effects on the solving process. The findings highlight Fable 5's superior raw problem-solving ability and suggest that the /goal feature modifies the search strategy rather than simply enhancing performance. All code, prompts, and results are publicly available for further examination.

items.title: Study analyzes 109 public Qubes OS security bulletins from 2011 to 2025, finding most vulnerabilities stem from upstream components like Xen and CPU microarchitecture
items.content_text: A longitudinal analysis of Qubes OS security bulletins reveals that nearly 80% of reported vulnerabilities are attributable to upstream components rather than Qubes core logic. The study covers 109 bulletins from 2011 to 2025 and uses various statistical methods to assess disclosure patterns and vulnerability discovery models. The research identifies a significant change point in early 2015, with disclosure rates stabilizing after 2018. Despite stable disclosure activity, the burden of vulnerabilities remains concentrated in trusted upstream components such as Xen hypervisor and CPU microarchitectural elements, highlighting ongoing dependency risks in Qubes OS security.

items.title: Netflix acquires Ben Affleck's AI startup InterPositive for $587 million to enhance filmmaking tools [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Netflix completed a $587 million acquisition of Ben Affleck's AI startup InterPositive, which develops AI tools to assist filmmakers by enhancing post-production processes like mixing, relighting, and visual effects. The deal, disclosed in a federal filing, brought InterPositive's 16-person team to Netflix, with Affleck joining as a senior adviser. Founded in 2022 and operating in stealth mode, InterPositive aims to keep filmmakers central to the creative process while leveraging AI technology. Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos highlighted the integration of generative AI tools in about 300 titles this year and noted that AI is used to improve efficiency without replacing human creativity.

items.title: Barracuda says AI-powered email spam filters are being bypassed by text salting, an old technique that hides malicious content with benign words [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Cybersecurity firm Barracuda reports that AI-based email filters are increasingly fooled by text salting, a decades-old method where attackers insert harmless-looking words to confuse machine learning models. Since April, Barracuda has detected over one million retail-themed phishing attacks using this technique, which can hide malicious content from AI while appearing normal to human readers. Text salting uses methods like CSS cropping, text manipulation, and zero font techniques to conceal filler text from humans but expose it to automated scanners, causing AI filters to misclassify emails as safe. While traditional email security systems have adapted to detect hidden text, many AI-driven tools lack this capability by default. Barracuda recommends a layered email security approach that includes sender reputation checks, authentication, URL analysis, and detection of hidden content to better protect enterprises from these attacks.

items.title: Talon launches a self-hosted platform to manage long-lived AI agents across multiple frontends and backends [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Talon is a multi-platform, self-hosted harness designed to deploy and control long-lived AI agents. It supports various frontends including Telegram, Discord, Microsoft Teams, terminal, and a cross-platform companion app, and integrates with multiple backends such as Claude Agent SDK, Kilo, OpenCode, Codex, and OpenAI Agents. The platform offers a modular architecture with features like session management, tool access, and background agent processes. It provides standalone binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows, and supports interactive setup and operation through command-line interfaces. Talon aims to facilitate persistent AI agent activity with flexible backend and frontend configurations.

items.title: Soofi consortium launches Soofi S, Europe's first industrial AI model focused on transparency and sovereignty, with 30B parameters and 27 trillion tokens [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: The Soofi consortium has introduced Soofi S, the first industrial AI model developed in Europe designed for transparent, adaptable, and sovereign AI applications in industrial settings. The model targets use cases requiring control and efficiency, such as technical documentation, code generation, and agent-based AI systems. Soofi S is a 30 billion parameter Mixture-of-Experts model trained on 27 trillion tokens, primarily in German and English, serving as the foundation for future specialized models. The consortium is currently conducting practical tests with industry partners and is seeking companies and organizations interested in trialing industrial AI applications.

items.title: New AI system generates speech in a thousand distinct voices to improve localization and voice synthesis applications [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A new artificial intelligence system has been developed that can generate speech in a thousand different voices, aiming to enhance voice synthesis and localization by capturing diverse vocal characteristics. This technology uses advanced machine learning to understand character traits, emotional nuances, and narrative context, enabling more natural and consistent voice performances across various applications. The system introduces the role of a Character Architect who defines detailed language profiles for characters, including speech patterns, emotional variations, and relationships, allowing the AI to produce dialogue that maintains character consistency over time. This approach contrasts with traditional machine translation workflows by focusing on quality and context rather than literal line-by-line translation, potentially benefiting industries like entertainment, accessibility, and communication.

items.title: Andreessen Horowitz hires Josh Elman from Apple to lead consumer AI startup investments amid AI boom [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Josh Elman, a veteran tech investor and former Apple AI team member, has joined Andreessen Horowitz to focus on consumer AI startups, departing Apple as the AI industry consolidates around major players like Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic. Elman believes the consumer AI market is poised for significant growth, comparing the current moment to the early dot-com era and anticipating a surge of innovative AI products beyond the dominant companies. Elman cited his experience at Apple and previous venture roles at Greylock and other tech firms, emphasizing that large companies can only excel at a limited number of AI applications, leaving opportunities for startups to develop specialized consumer AI agents. He expects consumer AI tools to evolve rapidly over the next two years, offering personalized assistance in areas such as travel and life management, challenging the notion that only major AI firms will lead the market.

items.title: Report: AI tools are negatively impacting job interview processes by altering candidate evaluation
items.content_text: AI technologies are increasingly being used in job interviews, but concerns are rising about their impact on the fairness and effectiveness of candidate assessments. The use of AI in this context may be changing how interviewers evaluate applicants, potentially leading to unintended consequences for hiring practices.

items.title: Trump revokes Biden-era AI regulations in 2025 aiming for industry growth; rising AI risks and public backlash lead to widespread data center moratoriums by mid-2026
items.content_text: In January 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order rolling back many of the Biden administration's AI safety regulations as part of a light-touch approach to foster industry growth. Joined by AI and crypto adviser David Sacks, Trump aimed to position the U.S. at the forefront of AI development. However, by mid-2026, the emergence of powerful AI models like Anthropic's Mythos has raised cybersecurity and economic concerns among various sectors, including banking and intelligence agencies. Public apprehension about AI's impact on jobs and energy costs has prompted over 300 states, cities, and counties to impose moratoriums on data center construction, challenging Trump's initial AI agenda.

items.title: PrimeTask launches offline-first work OS combining tasks, projects, CRM, calendar, and BYO AI integration via MCP [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: PrimeTask has introduced an offline-first work operating system that integrates task management, project planning, CRM, calendar, focus tools, and a visual canvas into a single desktop app. It supports Bring Your Own AI through MCP and offers deep Apple ecosystem integration, including bidirectional sync with Apple Reminders and Siri support. The system is designed for freelancers, consultants, and small businesses seeking a unified productivity platform they own rather than rent. The app features natural language task entry, multiple project views, custom fields, automations without monthly caps, and a visual canvas called PrimeFlow that connects projects, tasks, and contacts bidirectionally. PrimeTask emphasizes offline functionality with sync capabilities when online and aims to replace multiple subscriptions by consolidating productivity tools into one native Swift-built application.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol tops Design Arena leaderboard by avoiding common AI web design anti-patterns and improving speed and cost efficiency [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol achieved first place on Design Arena's Web Design leaderboard, outperforming its predecessor GPT-5.5 by 18 ranks. The model demonstrates a unique ability to recognize and avoid common AI design anti-patterns such as purple gradients, bento-box layouts, and oversized hero text, resulting in more refined and personalized web designs. GPT-5.6 Sol balances strong template use with high customization, setting new efficiency benchmarks by being over twice as fast as the previous leader GLM 5.2 and significantly cheaper than competitors like Claude Fable 5. Analysis of GPT-5.6 Sol's design outputs using CLIP embeddings and UMAP visualization revealed distinct gaps in its design space where typical AI-generated anti-patterns appear in earlier models. Unlike other models that avoid these patterns by excluding them from templates, GPT-5.6 Sol appears to have learned these anti-patterns but deliberately suppresses them in its outputs. This approach contributes to its superior ranking and suggests a more nuanced understanding of design quality in AI-generated web content.

items.title: Roblox launches Build, a mobile-first AI-powered creation tool enabling users to generate and publish games via text prompts starting July 28 in New Zealand [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Roblox announced Build, a new mobile-first creation tab within its app that uses AI to help users create games from text prompts. Starting July 28, Build will enter public alpha in New Zealand, allowing age-checked users 9 and older to generate basic games, which can be iterated on, playtested, and published after passing safety checks. Build integrates with Roblox Studio, enabling creators to enhance projects across platforms and access AI-powered tools for gameplay, environment, and character generation. Build leverages proprietary and open-source AI models trained on extensive 3D gaming data to produce functional 3D objects and scenes. Roblox plans to expand Build's availability and features over time, including advanced tools for professional creators such as playtesting agents, analytics, and experiment agents to improve engagement and monetization. Published games created with Build will undergo the same review and discovery processes as other Roblox games, ensuring quality and safety for users.

items.title: Teya launches open-source AI family agent for home use on wall-mounted Android phones [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Teya is an open-source AI family agent designed to run on inexpensive, wall-mounted Android phones, providing a shared intelligent presence that listens, understands, remembers, and assists with household tasks. It connects to cloud AI models via API calls, requiring no local server, and supports features like shopping lists, calendar management, reminders, expense tracking, and hands-free calls to approved contacts. The system aims to help manage the mental load of household logistics by acting as a second brain for the family, while maintaining privacy by operating on dedicated accounts separate from personal logins.

items.title: Akshay republishes and updates his 2002 thesis on the mathematical foundations of the Indic calendar system, clarifying its scientific basis and dispelling mystical misconceptions
items.content_text: Akshay has released a 20th anniversary edition of his undergraduate thesis originally written in 2002, which explores the mathematical principles behind the Indic calendar system using Vedanga Jyotisa and Surya Siddhanta. The thesis, previously hosted on his supervisor's university webpage, has been updated with embedded graphics and tables, and clarifies that the work is purely mathematical rather than mystical despite its title and some symbolic imagery. The thesis uses a fictional narrative inspired by ancient Indian mathematical texts to frame the research, which includes modeling calendar calculations in Java and LISP and comparing Indic, Chinese, and Islamic calendars. Akshay emphasizes the scientific nature of the work and its focus on calendar computations such as predicting Chinese New Year and Deepavali dates, distancing it from any association with black magic or tantra.

items.title: Guide details setting up a spare Mac to run Claude Code with full control and remote access via SSH and mobile app [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: A step-by-step guide explains how to configure a spare Mac to run Claude Code, an AI assistant, allowing users to control it remotely from their phone or main Mac. The setup involves creating a fresh local account on the spare Mac, enabling SSH for remote login, and configuring passwordless sudo to allow the AI agent to perform administrative tasks safely separated from the main machine. The guide emphasizes using a separate machine to mitigate risks associated with running Claude Code with broad permissions on a primary device. It also highlights advantages over containerized setups, such as full access to Mac-only applications and the ability to control the AI agent through the official Claude app. The instructions assume users have both a main and a spare Mac on the same network and provide detailed steps for wiping the spare Mac, setting up user accounts, and enabling remote control features.

items.title: Private Jets Are Scarce. Blame the Gusher of AI Wealth
items.content_text: After Bill Papariella, a Fort Lauderdale, Fla.-based entrepreneur, sold his private jet charter business for nearly $1 billion in 2022, he took it easy for a couple years. But as the number of ultrawealthy continued to climb in the U.S., another business idea struck him: a company that offered fractional jet ownership, like NetJets, but with a service designed as an even more premium product. Last October, he launched Bond, planning a private plane fleet with interiors lined in Loro Piana textiles, custom crystal from French brand Saint-Louis and cabin attendants on every flight. To give Bond a heightened sense of exclusivity, Papariella capped the company's initial membership at around 100 people, who pay between $1.1 million and $3.5 million a year depending on the aircraft. Its members have an average net worth of $500 million, and about 30% of them hail from Silicon Valley-founders, researchers and engineers at companies like xAI, Anthropic and OpenAI, many of them under the age of 34, Papariella said. (He wouldn't comment publicly on anyone's identity.) Flights on a fleet of 20 airplanes will begin in 2027. "The amount of influx we've had from the youth has been something I did not see coming," said Papariella, speaking from a yacht in the Mediterranean Sea recently. "That's only happened over the last two months."

Co-CEO Ted Sarandos put specific numbers to the effort: the docuseries "The American Experiment" includes 17 minutes of AI-assisted footage, produced twice as fast at half the cost. The savings will "likely" fund more content rather than shrink the $20 billion budget. items.title: Uber Does a Big Deal and Netflix's Growth Slows
items.content_text: Busy day. Uber unveiled its biggest-ever acquisition, the roughly $14 billion purchase of Delivery Hero, a German-based food-delivery giant with operations around the world. Netflix reported slower growth for the second quarter, as it had telegraphed, sending the stock down 8% to a two-year low. And SpaceX stock closed below its $135 a share IPO price for the first time, finishing the day at $131.11. Eek! We can get to Uber and Netflix in a minute, but we should acknowledge that SpaceX stock's drop coincided with a broader market sell-off that seems to afflict anyone with AI exposure. In other words, it's not necessarily a loss of confidence in Elon Musk's rocket ship firm. (The company is still valued at $1.7 trillion, which is a lot). The Nasdaq-100 index fell 1.6% on Thursday, with most major names losing ground. One way you can tell AI was the common theme-and we're only half-joking-is that Microsoft stock rose.

items.title: M&A Buzz Centers on Data Software Startups [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: We just published our list of more than 160 enterprise software startups that could be acquired this year. To compile it, we screened hundreds of privately held companies and singled out those worth more than $1 billion that haven't raised a publicly announced financing since June 2024. To understand the M&A forces across enterprise software, I spoke with more than 30 founders, investors, and bankers. The list has nearly doubled since we last put it together. The reason: as AI takes center stage, venture capitalists have shied from backing traditional software companies and are pouring their money into AI instead. Stock prices for publicly traded enterprise software companies have fallen at least 30% in the last year, dimming the older startups' prospects for an IPO-especially when SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI are seen to suck up much of the available investor demand.

items.title: Nobody is Immune From the Nvidia GPU Crunch [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Earlier this week, I wrote about startups moving some of their workloads from Amazon Web Services and other traditional cloud providers to young challengers such as Nebius. That's in part because startups are having trouble getting the Nvidia chips they need on AWS, sometimes because those chips are only available in too expensive packages. Capacity can be so scarce that an Nvidia representative told one small AI startup it should rent spare GPUs from an Asia-based facility it knew about, an executive at the startup told us.
